    What the text on a card says

    One card of each of the three card types, as text. The app’s own sample cards. The artwork is made in ChatGPT from the prompts the app writes.

    Full game24 cards
    10Real or Bluff
    8Spot the Fake
    6Invent the Bluff
    Short game12 cards (5 · 4 · 3)
    Real or Bluff2 points

    Bread Bubbles

    “Bread dough rises because the yeast in it gives off tiny bubbles of oxygen gas.”

    BLUFF Yeast gives off carbon dioxide, not oxygen. The gas gets trapped in the dough and makes it puff up.
    Why it fools people: oxygen is the gas everyone has heard of, so it feels right.

    The reader says a statement. Players bet whether it is real or a bluff.

    Spot the Fake2 points

    Rainbow Facts

    • A A rainbow forms when sunlight is bent and reflected inside raindrops.
    • B Red appears on the outer edge of a main rainbow.
    • C A rainbow forms when sunlight is bent by clouds of dust high above the rain.
    • D Each person sees a slightly different rainbow, depending on where they stand.
    C is the fake. Rainbows come from raindrops, not dust. Every viewer sees their own rainbow from where they stand.

    Four statements, one is fake. Players find it.

    Invent the Bluff2 points

    Window Droplets

    What does Condensation mean?

    • A Tiny water droplets that form when warm, damp air touches a cold surface.
    • B The slow wearing away of rock by flowing water over a long time.
    • C A thick layer of frost that builds up inside a freezer.
    A is the real definition. The cold glass cools the damp air nearby, and the water vapor turns back into liquid drops.

    One real definition and made-up decoys. Players write or pick the bluff.

    For every card it also writes a headline, a reveal text, why it fools people, an image idea for ChatGPT and a flag when a fact needs checking. You keep control: you check the facts and approve each image.
